- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next 3–5 days.
- When sentiment is consistently negative (≤-0.33), model underestimates; increase forecast by 1–3% for next 3–5 days.
- After a sharp price spike (≥5% from prior peak), model often overshoots; cap forecast at +3% above peak for 3–7 days.
- If model forecast is >10% above recent 18-day average, reduce by 2–5% if sentiment is neutral or negative.
- If model forecast is <10% below recent 18-day average, increase by 1–3% if sentiment is positive or neutral.
- Model tends to lag in early days of sentiment shift; adjust forecast 1–2 days ahead of sentiment change direction.
- For 30-day horizon, model often overestimates mean reversion; reduce forecast by 1–2% if sentiment is weak or mixed.
- If sentiment history shows alternating +/– signals, model tends to average out; use sentiment-weighted moving average for smoothing.
